name: Threat Modelling for Agents
question: What can go wrong, and where can it come in?
summary: List what the agent can read, what it can do and where its output can go, then map each capability to known risks: the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025) and the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026). The quickest test is the lethal trifecta: an agent that combines private data, untrusted content and a way to communicate externally can be steered into leaking that data. Remove or gate one leg.
useCases: Before an agent gets real data, real tools or real users
Whenever a new tool, data source or output channel is added
Security reviews and regulator questions in BFSI and healthcare

Mark every point where untrusted text enters the context
Map each capability to OWASP LLM and ASI risks
Remove or gate one leg of every trifecta, and record the residual risk
pitfalls: Treating prompt injection as solved by a better system prompt
Giving the agent the user’s full token when one scope would do
Forgetting that rendered output (links, images) is an outbound channel
remember: Private data, untrusted content, a way out: never all three unguarded.

steps.title: Inventory every capability
steps.text: Write down what the agent can read, what it can do and every way output leaves: data sources, tools with their scopes, and channels, including how the chat renders replies.

steps.title: Mark the trust boundaries
steps.text: Uploaded PDFs and forwarded emails can be written by anyone. Everything that enters from them is untrusted, whoever the user is.

steps.title: Map capabilities to OWASP risks
steps.text: Untrusted inputs map to prompt injection (LLM01) and goal hijack (ASI01), outbound channels to information disclosure (LLM02), and actions to excessive agency (LLM06) and tool misuse (ASI02).

steps.title: Count the trifecta paths
steps.text: Each combination of private data, untrusted input and ungated outbound channel is a path for theft: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 here.

steps.title: Remove or gate one leg
steps.text: Rendering plain text only closes the image channel, and human approval gates the email tool. No ungated path remains.

steps.title: Record the residual risk
steps.text: Each remaining risk gets a control, a residual rating and a named owner, and a CI check fails if a new ungated path appears.

practice.scenario: A private bank is about to launch a UPI assistant. It can read a customer’s statements and uploaded PDFs, search forwarded emails, look up payees, start transfers to saved beneficiaries, and reply in a chat that renders markdown. Before any code review, the security team inventories these capabilities as code, finds two lethal trifectas, and maps each capability to OWASP LLM and ASI risks.

industries.use: Inventory data, tools and channels for a payments assistant before launch
Map a patient-portal agent’s record access and outbound messages to risks
Review a support agent that reads tickets from anyone and can email customers

practice.analogy: Walking a new building with a fire officer: where can fire start, how does it spread, and where are the exits? You find the risks on paper before anyone moves in.

library.name: Threat model as code (Python + YAML)
library.what: Keep the capability inventory in a reviewed file and check it automatically for trifectas on every change.

practice.note: Treat the inventory like code: a pull request that adds a tool or channel must update it, and the trifecta check runs in CI.

samples.code:
import yaml

INVENTORY = yaml.safe_load("""
data:      [statements, payees, balances]           # private data
untrusted: [uploaded_pdfs, forwarded_emails]        # anyone can write these
outbound:  [markdown_images, email_tool]            # ways out
actions:   [transfer_to_saved_payee]
gates:     {email_tool: human_approval}
""")

OWASP = {"untrusted": ["LLM01 Prompt Injection", "ASI01 Agent Goal Hijack"],
         "outbound":  ["LLM02 Sensitive Information Disclosure"],
         "actions":   ["LLM06 Excessive Agency", "ASI02 Tool Misuse"]}

def trifectas(inv):
    gated = set(inv.get("gates", {}))
    open_out = [o for o in inv["outbound"] if o not in gated]
    return [(d, u, o) for d in inv["data"] for u in inv["untrusted"] for o in open_out]

paths = trifectas(INVENTORY)
print(f"{len(paths)} ungated trifecta paths")      # 3 × 2 × 1 = 6, all via markdown images
for part, risks in OWASP.items():
    print(part, "→", ", ".join(risks))

numericDrill.question: An agent can read 3 kinds of private data, takes in 2 kinds of untrusted content, and has 2 ungated ways to send data out. How many distinct (private data, untrusted content, outbound channel) trifecta paths does it have?
numericDrill.answer: 3 × 2 × 2 = 12 paths. Gating one outbound channel with approval halves them to 6; gating both removes them all, which is why controls on the way out are so effective.

interview.question: What is the lethal trifecta, and why does it matter?
interview.answer: It is the combination of access to private data, exposure to untrusted content and a way to communicate externally. If an agent has all three, instructions hidden in the untrusted content can make it send the private data out. Removing or gating any one leg breaks that path, which is more reliable than trying to detect every injection.

interview.question: How do the two OWASP lists differ?
interview.answer: The Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025) covers risks of LLM-based applications in general, such as prompt injection, sensitive information disclosure and excessive agency. The Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026) focuses on autonomous agents: goal hijack, tool misuse, identity and privilege abuse, supply chain, code execution, memory poisoning, inter-agent communication, cascading failures, human trust exploitation and rogue agents. Use both to cover an agent.

mistakes.mistake: Threat modelling once at design time
mistakes.fix: Update the inventory whenever a tool, data source or channel changes
List rendering (images, links) as an outbound channel

quiz.question: A UPI assistant reads customers’ statements, summarises PDFs they upload, and its chat renders images from any URL. Which risk pattern does this combination create?
options: The lethal trifecta: private data, untrusted content and a way out
quiz.explanation: Private data plus untrusted content plus an outbound channel lets injected text steal the data.

quiz.question: Which OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025) entry covers an attacker’s instructions hidden in a document the model reads?
quiz.explanation: Indirect injection is a form of prompt injection, LLM01.

quiz.question: An agent can move money with the customer’s full session token even for read-only questions. Which OWASP LLM risk is this?
quiz.explanation: More permissions or autonomy than the task needs is excessive agency.

quiz.question: An agent has 3 private data sources, 2 untrusted inputs and 2 ungated outbound channels. How many trifecta paths?
Which of these count as outbound channels in a threat model? Select all that apply.
options: Markdown images the chat client renders
quiz.explanation: Anything that can carry data to a destination outside, including rendering, is outbound; prompts and questions are inputs.

quiz.question: The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications was published when?
quiz.explanation: It was released in December 2025 as the 2026 edition.

quiz.question: Which ASI entry covers an attacker redirecting an agent’s objective or plan?
Which is the most reliable way to deal with a lethal trifecta?
options: Remove or gate one of the three legs
quiz.explanation: Breaking any leg removes the path; prompts only lower the odds.

quiz.question: A fintech adds a web-browsing tool to its account assistant. Which threat-model updates follow? Select all that apply.
options: Web pages become a new untrusted input
The browsing tool may be a new outbound channel through URLs
Nothing changes because the tool is read-only
quiz.explanation: Reading web pages adds untrusted content, and fetching URLs can carry data out.

quiz.question: Why should chat rendering be in the capability inventory?
options: Rendered images and links are fetched by the client, so they can carry data out
quiz.explanation: An image URL can leak data with no click.

quiz.question: Which ASI entry covers third-party tools, frameworks and registries carrying exposure?
quiz.explanation: Supply-chain exposure through components is ASI04.

quiz.question: Which gates break the trifecta for a statement-reading assistant that renders images? Select all that apply.
options: Render text only, with no untrusted images
A separated reader so untrusted text cannot steer the tool-using model
Asking the model politely to be careful
Adding more examples to the prompt
quiz.explanation: Closing the channel or separating the reader removes the path; prompt changes do not.

quiz.question: An agent writes customer notes to long-term memory, including text from uploaded documents. Which ASI risk is most relevant?
quiz.explanation: Stored untrusted text can steer future sessions.

quiz.question: A threat model was written at design time. Six months later, three tools have been added. What is the main problem?
options: The inventory no longer matches the agent, so new paths are unmapped
quiz.explanation: Update the inventory whenever capabilities change, ideally checked in CI.

quiz.question: Which belong in a residual-risk register entry? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: Risk, control, residual rating and owner make it actionable.

quiz.question: An agent only reads public product pages and answers anonymous shoppers, with no personal data or tools. Which trifecta leg is missing?
quiz.explanation: Without private data there is nothing to steal, though other risks such as misinformation remain.

quiz.question: Which ASI entry covers an agent’s identity or permissions being misused or escalated?
quiz.explanation: Identity and privilege abuse is ASI03.

quiz.question: A patient-portal agent can read records and send secure messages to any address. Which changes reduce risk most? Select all that apply.
options: Restrict messages to the patient’s verified address
Scope record access to the current patient
Allow messages to any address but log them
quiz.explanation: Gating the outbound channel and scoping data shrink both the path and the blast radius.

quiz.question: Which resource describes adversary tactics and techniques against AI systems, with case studies?
quiz.explanation: ATLAS is MITRE’s knowledge base for AI threats.

quiz.question: What does the OWASP LLM entry LLM10 Unbounded Consumption cover?
options: Excessive or uncontrolled use of resources, cost and inference
quiz.explanation: It covers resource exhaustion and cost abuse.
